links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition, chapter 5: Debugging
links.why: The textbook chapter this course chapter follows.

links.title: Logging HOWTO
links.why: The basic tutorial, the levels and the lazy-formatting advice, from the interpreter's own docs.

links.title: logging — Logging facility for Python
links.why: Reference for basicConfig, disable and the level numbers.

links.title: pdb — The Python Debugger
links.why: Every debugger command, including step, next, return, continue, break and where.

links.title: 7. Simple statements — the assert statement
links.why: The exact meaning of assert, including why it produces no code under optimisation.

links.title: 7. Simple statements — the raise statement
links.why: What raise does and how exceptions chain.

links.title: Built-in Exceptions
links.why: AssertionError, the exception hierarchy, add_note and __notes__.

links.title: traceback — Print or retrieve a stack traceback
links.why: Read and format tracebacks from a program.

links.title: 8. Errors and Exceptions
links.why: The tutorial's account of raising, handling and enriching exceptions.

links.title: 1. Command line and environment
links.why: The -O option and the PYTHONBREAKPOINT variable.

links.title: PEP 553 – Built-in breakpoint()
links.why: Why breakpoint() exists and how sys.breakpointhook is used.

links.title: PEP 657 – Include Fine Grained Error Locations in Tracebacks
links.why: The carets under the failing part of a line.

links.title: PEP 678 – Enriching Exceptions with Notes
links.why: add_note and __notes__.

links.title: PEP 768 – Safe external debugger interface for CPython
links.why: How Python 3.14 lets a debugger attach to a running process.

links.title: Python Tutor
links.why: Paste a program and step through it line by line in the browser, with the variables drawn.

links.title: Logging Cookbook
links.why: Worked recipes for logging to files, several handlers and formats, after the basics of the Logging HOWTO.

links.title: PEP 282 – A Logging System
links.why: The 2002 proposal by Vinay Sajip and Trent Mick behind the five log levels (story: a logging system with a birth certificate).

links.title: Software bug (with the 1947 Mark II logbook page)
links.why: The history of the word bug, including the moth taped into the Harvard Mark II logbook on 9 September 1947.

links.title: Brian Kernighan
links.why: Biography and bibliography of the author of the 1979 sentence on careful thought and print statements.

links.title: Mu, a Python editor for beginners
links.why: The editor whose debugger the textbook chapter uses.
